basis: a7m3_map FINDINGS.md M3-F030..F048, modding/OG_M3_V2.md (static analysis and emulation of the 4.04 update; nine camera runs, three clips measured)

predictions.claim: SET_FILE2 of /tmp/jiritsu/libJit.so answers status 0 and the camera loads the library (the result file exists afterwards). Medium-high: the route is verified statically (M3-F011) and the file route with MOUNT works (M3-F032), but no code has been loaded on an A7 III yet.
v2: the result is created on /tmp_network (a 1 MB RAM tmpfs seen in /proc/mounts in service mode); if that fails, in /tmp/jiritsu. Either is read back and deleted.
euid is 0 (root) and /dev/mem opens.
predictions.source: libJiritsu.so opens /dev/mem itself; A7 IV F409

predictions.claim: v2: the LIRO header at phys 0x035C6000 and the two code ranges (imager_code, fe_selector_code) are SAME as the 4.04 file; some of the first 16 image pages differ (live data, reported only). High: seen in all three v1 sessions.
On a stock camera after a battery pull the dump says VERDICT READY (stock), and /proc/cmdline equals kemco.txt of the 4.04 update.

test1 answers DONE (7 bytes in 4 runs) and READY (test 1 applied). In 4K 24p full frame the live view then shows a picture moved by about 312 sensor rows (about 9 percent of the frame height) towards one edge of the sensor: the front end keeps cropping the first 3376 rows of a now 4036-row read. Low-medium for the camera's behaviour: the front end receives 624 more lines per frame than its record expects; a frozen or garbled picture, or a restart, is possible and is itself the answer.

test2 answers DONE and READY (test 2 applied). In 4K 24p full frame the live view and the clip show the whole 3:2 sensor height squeezed into 16:9 (round things look 1.185 times wider), the file stays 3840x2160. Low: the front end's 65 vertical fields per record were moved by formula, not seen on a camera; focus areas and statistics may sit off.
putback answers DONE and READY (stock); a battery pull also restores 4.04 (the warm-boot image reloads av-cam). The power switch alone may NOT reset RAM (A7S family: it is a suspend).
predictions.source: A7s Claude A7S-F15/F16, JOURNAL OG2 run

predictions.claim: The dump reports the TV system of the 4K full-frame drive from the runtime drive table (59.94: slot 28 on the first tester's camera) and six blocks STOCK; the runtime cycle pair reads 836 / 1718 and the derived byte 38. High: these bytes were in the v2 dumps.

test2 (v3: sensor + records + timing pair 726 / 2030) answers DONE and READY (test 2 applied). In 4K 24p full frame the picture is the whole 3:2 height squeezed 1.185. Low-medium: the pair is the one stock quantity that v2 left inconsistent, but the line rate is 15 % above any stock mode and other camera-core fields (size row, record words of variant 0x19) are untouched. A restart like v2's is possible and restores stock.

If test2 restarts the camera, test3 (+312 rows, pair 787 / 1874, line rate +6 %) or test4 (+156 rows, pair 821 / 1796, +2 %) gives a picture. If all three restart, the cycle pair is not the missing piece (or not the only one).

After a forced restart the application log ring (phys 0x03524FC0, 0x60040 bytes) read by the next dump still holds av-cam's lines from before the restart, among them "S-Ele Refresh!" and one of "Lost CAMOUT_V ...", "RCV overflow VD Seq Refresh!" or "SDVGA_SRC overflow VD Seq Refresh!". Medium-low: the ring lies inside a warm-boot memory range (wbimem 0x500000@0x03085000), so the restart may overwrite it; the kernel log ring outside that range did survive.

norestart sets bit 0x40 of byte 0x6433cd5e (stock value expected 0x00) and reads it back. With test 4 + norestart the camera stays on in movie mode; the picture may hiccup at each refresh (the loop re-sends the sensor state). Medium: the bit is tested right before the forced stop (ands r7,#0x40 at 0x6393578a), but nothing has shown yet that the byte keeps its value while the camera runs.

The dump after that movie try reads a refresh counter (0x643548dc) far above 10 and the sticky byte 0x64688aa9 = 1 (the lost-CAMOUT_V path ran). Low-medium: the alternatives are the status byte 0x6433aa4f bits 0x81 or the overflow flags 0x64688ab7/ab8.

With nocheck (bit 0x02) the picture is steady in movie mode at test 4 and at test 2, and the clip records. Low-medium: the picture was seen for a second with the loop running, so frames do arrive; whether every frame arrives is not known.

A dump taken with the dial left on movie holds the last movie frame: SGC1 cycle 525 x 2860 (59.94 system) or 525 x 2740, window registers 373 / 1706 in stock, and a CamOutV stamp a few seconds old at most. Medium: seen so far only with the dial on stills, where the phase (CamV - CamOutV modulo the frame) repeated to three decimals in three dumps.

The output sync comes later in the frame with test 4 than in stock, and later again with test 2, by about the extra read-out time (156 and 624 rows at 7.29 us: 1.1 ms and 4.6 ms), and with a test + norestart the frozen refresh counter is far above 10. Low-medium: this is the reading that the sync follows the end of the sensor read-out; if the phase does not move, the cause is elsewhere.

test3 (v6: +92 rows, pair 836 / 1764, line period stock) with norestart on a 59.94 camera: the picture is smooth, the refresh counter in the movie-dial dump is 0 and the two frame counters are equal. Low-medium. If it holds, the shortened line period is what breaks tests 2 and 4. If it stutters with a non-zero counter, the line count or the record heights are.

In the movie-dial dump after test3 (+92 rows) the output sync reads about 22.497 to 22.498 ms after the frame start, 6 to 7 microseconds later than stock (22.491). Medium: the v5 figures give 0.070 and 0.075 microseconds per extra row (+11 at 156 rows, +47 at 624), and the stamps repeated to 1 microsecond in three stills dumps. Reading the outcome: stutter with a refresh count above 0 clears the shortened line period and leaves the line count / the slip; smooth with a count of 0 leaves two readings (the line period is the fault, or a slip of 7 microseconds is still tolerated and 11 is not), which a +92-row step with a shortened period would split.

test5 (test 3 + size row inner height 3468, read-out words 6474) answers DONE and READY (test 5 applied) on a camera: every stock byte of the four new blocks was checked against both testers' dumps (3376, 3376, 6302 or 6308). In the recorded clip the picture then reaches the last row (2159) with no black band, the refresh counter in the movie-dial dump is 0 and the two frame counters are equal. Low-medium: the size row is the one stock quantity left that states the picture height, but no code path from it to the last sensor row has been traced. If the picture still ends at row 2136 with the band, the size row is not what sets the last row. Any other row is new information (for example 2159 minus a few: a second, smaller limit).

test6 (test 3 with the first row at 281) with norestart at 24p: the recorded frame is whole (picture to row 2159, no black band, no strip), the refresh counter in the movie-dial dump is 0 and the two frame counters are equal. Medium-low. It follows from the one rule that fits tests 3, 4 and 5 to the row (valid lines = stock crop + half the added rows = the stock last sensor row 3785), but that rule also fits the other reading, that only half of the row-count change takes effect; in that case the frame ends at row 2136 again. A picture that ends between the two would mean a limit of its own.
